entryPoint: SLA::isTransient() in include/class.sla.php (lines 95-97): `function isTransient() { return $this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT; }`. Self-contained inline bitwise-AND expression against SLA::FLAG_TRANSIENT (0x0008, defined line 30 as part of the packed `flags` bitmask column also holding FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0001, FLAG_ESCALATE=0x0002, FLAG_NOALERTS=0x0004). No sub-delegation, no argument.
coreLogic: The entire logic is the single expression `$this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT` — no delegation chain, no helper method calls. Note this is a bitwise AND (not the logical `&&` bug seen in SLA::priorityEscalation()/MOD-26), so it correctly isolates only the FLAG_TRANSIENT bit. It returns the raw int result of that AND (0 when unset, 8 when set) rather than a double-negated strict bool — matching the style of SLA::isActive() (line 91-93, same file) and the `$base['transient']` line in SLA::getInfo() (line 85), and distinct from Dept::isActive()'s `!!(...)` pattern used in the MOD-32 extraction. This exact non-bool-coerced return value must be preserved.
consumers: Ticket::transfer(TransferForm $form, &$errors, $alert=true) in include/class.ticket.php line 2663: `if (!$this->getSLAId() || $this->getSLA()->isTransient()) if (($slaId=$this->getDept()->getSLAId())) $this->selectSLAId($slaId);` — after a department transfer, if the ticket has no SLA id set OR its currently loaded SLA is transient, re-derives the SLA from the new (target) department's configured SLA id.

Ticket::update($vars, &$errors) in include/class.ticket.php line 3767: `if (!$keepSLA && (!$this->getSLA() || $this->getSLA()->isTransient())) { $this->selectSLAId(); }` — where `$keepSLA = ($this->getSLAId() != $vars['slaId'])` was computed earlier (line 3708) BEFORE `$this->sla_id = $vars['slaId']` is assigned (line 3711); so `$keepSLA` is true when staff explicitly changed the SLA in the edit form. When the SLA was NOT explicitly changed (`!$keepSLA`) and the (now-reloaded, since `$this->sla_id` was just reassigned to the submitted value) SLA is missing or transient, calls the no-arg `selectSLAId()` to re-derive the SLA from dept → topic → system-default precedence.
inputShape: None — isTransient() takes no parameters. It reads the instance property $this->flags, an already-loaded packed int bitmask column on the SLA ORM row (VerySimpleModel). Both call sites first obtain the SLA object via Ticket::getSLA() (returns $this->sla, an ORM-resolved relation) and guard against a null SLA before calling isTransient(), so the method itself never needs to handle a null/missing SLA — it only runs on a real, loaded SLA instance.
outputShape: int — the raw result of `$this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT` (0 when the bit is unset, 8 when set), NOT a strictly-typed bool. Both consumers use the return value only in short-circuit boolean (`||`, `&&`) truthy/falsy contexts inside `if` conditions — neither performs a strict `=== true`/`=== false` comparison — so this loose-int truthiness is caller-visible-safe but must not be 'corrected' to `(bool)`/`!!` during extraction.
sideEffects: None. isTransient() performs no DB read/write, no global state access ($cfg, $thisstaff, etc.), no lazy-loading (contrast with SLA::getSchedule(), which lazily loads $this->_schedule), no caching, and no file I/O. It is a pure read of the already-in-memory $this->flags property.
constraints: Method signature `isTransient()` (no parameters) on class SLA must remain unchanged.

Must preserve returning the raw bitwise-AND int result (0 or 8), not a double-negated/cast strict bool — this differs from the DepartmentActiveChecker (MOD-32) precedent which uses `!!(...)`; isTransient() must follow the SLA::isActive()/getInfo() precedent instead (plain `&`, no coercion).

Must isolate only the FLAG_TRANSIENT bit (0x0008) via bitwise AND against SLA::flags — must NOT reproduce the logical-`&&` truthy-on-any-bit bug that SlaPriorityEscalationChecker (MOD-26) intentionally preserved for SLA::priorityEscalation(); isTransient()'s existing implementation is already correctly bitwise, so extraction must keep it bitwise.

The extracted service must never call back into SLA::isTransient() (the facade entry point it replaces) or any other SLA instance method, to avoid recursion once the facade delegates to it — per the repo's anti-recursion strangler pattern, it should accept the raw `flags` int as a parameter (mirroring SlaPriorityEscalationChecker::priorityEscalation($flags) and DepartmentActiveChecker::isActive($flags)), not the SLA object itself.

FLAG_TRANSIENT's value (0x0008) and its independence from FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0001), FLAG_ESCALATE (0x0002), and FLAG_NOALERTS (0x0004) must be preserved — setting any of those other bits alongside/instead of FLAG_TRANSIENT must not affect the result.

Facade-side null/existence guards on the SLA object (both call sites check `!$this->getSLA()` before calling isTransient()) are caller-side (Ticket) concerns, out of scope for this seam — the extracted service and facade patch touch only SLA::isTransient() and must not alter Ticket::transfer()/Ticket::update() call-site logic.
Do not touch SLA::addGracePeriod (MOD-25), SLA::priorityEscalation (MOD-26), ticket overdue/escalation helpers (MOD-27), or Ticket::assign (MOD-28) — this seam is isolated strictly to isTransient().
harnessInputShape: A single JSON field: `flags` (int) — the raw packed SLA::flags bitmask value to set on a bootstrapped SLA instance (via `SLA::create()` then `$sla->flags = $input['flags']`) before calling `$sla->isTransient()`. Test values should cover: FLAG_TRANSIENT alone (8, expect truthy), 0 (expect falsy), FLAG_TRANSIENT combined with each other flag bit (FLAG_ACTIVE=1, FLAG_ESCALATE=2, FLAG_NOALERTS=4) and all-combined (15), and each other flag bit alone without FLAG_TRANSIENT (expect falsy) — to prove only bit 0x0008 drives the result regardless of the other bits' state.
